title: Cash shifts, payables, receivables, owner dashboards & risk
summary: Drawer-per-counter shifts with verified cash drops, AP/AR, live P&L from the ledger, heuristic risk review.
markdown:
# Finance, owner dashboards & risk

## Shift-based cash (§7.1)

1. Counter staff: `POST /finance/cash-shifts/open {"node": "MainReception", "opening_float": 5000}` — every
   cash movement (registration, lab/pharmacy payment, refunds) goes through **your** open shift.
   **The float is part of the drawer.** It is issued from the main vault and is the drawer's first entry
   (`OpeningFloat` in `GET /finance/cash-shifts/{id}/transactions` and in `by_type`), so `expected_cash` starts at
   the float: 5000 before the first sale, 6000 after a cash sale of 1000, 4000 after a cash refund of 1000 with no sale.
   Show `expected_cash` as the server gives it; never add or subtract the float yourself. A payout bigger than the
   drawer holds, float included: `INSUFFICIENT_DRAWER_CASH`.
   The node is the PC's counter (`GET /terminals/whoami` `cash_node`). The pharmacy's cash goes only into a shift
   at the Pharmacy Counter (decisions 51): the pharmacists open theirs from the Pharmacy workspace, where My cash shift
   is listed too, and check it with `GET /finance/cash-shifts/mine?node=PharmacyCounter`
   ([the pharmacy's cash drawer](clinical-and-prescriptions.md)).
2. End of shift: the cashier counts **everything in the drawer, the float included**:
   `POST /finance/cash-shifts/{id}/close {"declared_cash"}` → `PendingCollection`. The answer's `declared_variance`
   (declared minus expected) shows a difference at once: a drawer of 5000 float and no movement declared as 0 is
   −5000, never a clean close.
3. Accountant counts the whole drawer, float included: `POST /finance/cash-shifts/{id}/cash-drop {"counted_cash", "note"}`.
   All of it goes to the main vault (the next shift is issued a fresh float), and the shift's `expected_cash` reads 0
   from then on; `cash_drop.expected_cash` and `cash_drop.variance` keep what was compared, and `declared_variance`
   still compares the cashier's count with what the drawer held at the close.
   At or above `large_cash_settlement_threshold` (in `GET /meta/settings`: show the fields before the first attempt) a
   **second, different approver** must co-sign (`second_approver_username/password`) or the drop waits in `/approvals`. Variances post to *Cash
   over/short* and are flagged. You can't verify your own drop.

## Accounts payable (§5.5, §6.9, §8.1)

Work orders, utility bills, visiting-consultant commissions and supplier invoices create payables.
`GET /finance/ap/queue` → hand over cash/bank → `POST /finance/ap/{ap_id}/settle {"method": "Cash", "cash_source": "Vault"}`
(amount defaults to the open balance). Settling closes the source (work order → Paid, commission → Paid).

**Credit notes for stock returned to suppliers** (decisions 47). The pharmacy admin returns stock to a supplier; the
accountant (never the same person: `DUAL_CONTROL_SAME_PERSON`) then deals with the supplier's answer:

1. `GET /pharmacy-admin/supplier-returns?status=Returned`: the returns awaiting a credit note, each with
   `value_at_cost`.
2. The credit note arrives: `POST /finance/supplier-returns/{return_id}/credit {"credit_note_no": "CN-2231",
   "credit_note_date": "2026-10-20", "credit_amount": 3800}`. A credit below the value at cost leaves the difference as
   a write-off. The supplier gives nothing: `POST /finance/supplier-returns/{return_id}/refuse {"note": "…"}` writes
   the claim off. Either one only once (`SUPPLIER_RETURN_STATE_INVALID` after).
3. The credit pays that supplier's bills: `POST /finance/ap/{ap_id}/settle {"method": "SupplierCredit",
   "supplier_return_id": 12, "amount": 3800}`. No money moves; `credit_left` goes down
   (`SUPPLIER_CREDIT_UNAVAILABLE` for another supplier's bill, a return not credited, or more than is left).

## Receivables / Udhaar (§1.9)

`GET /finance/ar/outstanding`, `GET /finance/ar/aging`, collect `POST /finance/ar/{id}/settle`, write off
(owner) `POST /finance/ar/{id}/write-off`.

The screen belongs to the cashier's workspace, and the Owner's workspace also uses it (`also_uses` of
`GET /meta/workspaces`): the Owner and the Hospital Admin open it from their own workspace, where `GET /meta/handbook`
lists it with the tasks they may do (the lists, the invoice and the write-off; never collecting or settling, which needs
a cash shift). Put it in their workspace's navigation from that answer, as for any other screen.

## Prices & policies (§7.2)

Service catalogue, panels & panel discounts, per-role/user discount ceilings
(`PUT /finance/discount-policies`), consultant contracts. Prices are snapshotted into every
ticket/invoice line — changing a price never alters history.
A service's department from `GET /admin/departments`; a ceiling for one user names them from `GET /staff/lookup` (their
`user_id`).

## Owner dashboard (§7.4)

* `GET /reports/pnl-flash?date_from&date_to` (default **today**, live): income per stream (OPD, IPD,
  pharmacy, lab, imaging, OT, rooms), discounts/refunds, expenses by category (COGS, commissions,
  utilities, repairs…), payroll **run-rate**, net profit, cash collected, open AR/AP.
* `GET /reports/pnl-trend?days=30` for charts; `GET /reports/patient-volume` — **Visited** (tickets) vs
  **Examined**, per doctor and hospital-wide (attrition = paid but never seen).
  Visited counts tickets whose fee was settled; `issued_unpaid` counts the ones never paid.
* Ledger: `GET /finance/gl/trial-balance`, `GET /finance/gl/ledger`.
* Holiday calendar (Hospital Admin, shared with HR): `GET /holidays`, `POST /holidays`, `PATCH /holidays/{id}`
  (screen `holiday_calendar_admin`). Fixed-schedule staff are off, paid, on a holiday; rostered staff work. Details:
  [HR, provisioning, attendance, leave & payroll](hr-and-payroll.md).

## Risk & compliance (§7.5)

`GET /risk/summary`, `GET /risk/findings`, review `POST /risk/findings/{id}/review {"status": "Resolved", "note"}`.
Findings are heuristics for human review — word them as "flagged for review". Rules include
voided-but-examined (critical), clinical edits after death/discharge, orphaned pharmacy deductions,
rapid re-routes without notes, excessive voids/refunds (waivers excluded), discount abuse, unreconciled
cash, unapproved charity, OT settlement gaps and payments without ledger postings.
